## How did Halloween become an American tradition?

The modern celebration of Halloween occurs every year on October 31. This Halloween tradition actually originated from the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain. During that time, people believed spirits returned to the physical world. When millions of Irish immigrants arrived in the United States during the nineteenth century, they brought these rich customs with them. This wave of new arrivals helped popularize the holiday nationally. Over the decades, the focus shifted away from superstition and witchcraft. By the turn of the century, communities actively encouraged friendly neighborhood gatherings instead. Today, it stands as the second-largest commercial holiday in the country, with citizens spending an estimated US$6 billion annually. People of all ages host festive parties to share sweet treats and show off their creative costumes. Yes. The centuries-old practice of trick-or-treating remains a staple of the season. Students who choose to [learn English in the USA](https://www.englishcollege.com/learn-english-usa) get to witness this incredible cultural transformation firsthand.

The familiar custom of going house to house actually evolved significantly over the years. Early colonial celebrations in New England were extremely limited due to rigid Protestant beliefs, though the event found more popularity in Maryland and southern colonies. Between 1920 and 1950, town leaders successfully revived trick-or-treating as an inexpensive way for entire neighborhoods to celebrate together. This specific time period also saw gatherings move from civic centers into classrooms and homes to accommodate the baby boom generation. Rather than playing pranks, neighbors provided small treats to local children. It worked. This simple exchange formed the foundation of the modern Halloween holiday we recognize today. The practice grew rapidly across the nation. You might be surprised by some historical facts about this famous Halloween night. Before pumpkins became the standard, people originally carved their jack-o-lanterns out of turnips, beets, and potatoes. In some American towns, the evening was even referred to as Cabbage Night. Another fascinating detail involves the sheer volume of candy collected by children. A typical child finishes the night with a loot bag containing approximately 11,000 calories. ### Why do people wear costumes on Halloween?

The tradition of dressing up began centuries ago as a practical measure against the supernatural. Ancient people would wear frightening masks to ward off evil spirits they believed crossed into the physical world. Young women also believed they could predict the appearance of their future husbands using tricks with yarn or apple parings. As the event modernized, newspapers and community leaders pushed to remove the grotesque elements. They succeeded. The focus shifted entirely toward fun, festive attire. Today, you will see everything from superheroes to classic ghosts walking down the street.
